messages:
maria: Observed a throughput cliff on the paged-attn path when we warm KV caches on SM90 boxes running CUDA 13.1. Short repro below.
ankit: Hmm, cliff as in qps drop? numbers?
maria: Yes, 2100 -> ~600 rps for batch_size=8, long_ctx=14k after ~30s of steady traffic. Latency spikes and GPU util drops.
sasha: Any regressions from kernel mux or selector flips? Triton vs native CUDA?
maria: Selector log shows it switched from fused_paged_flash -> flash_unfused mid-run. That correlates with the cliff.
ankit: Did selector log why it switched? scratch estimates, mem pressure, or some runtime flag?
maria: Ran with REDWOOD_KERNEL_LOG=1 and --kernel-policy=heuristic. Excerpt: 
```
selector: model=redwood/xxl seq=14000 bsz=8 arch=sm90 cuda=13.1 -> candidates: fused_paged_flash(score=720), flash_unfused(score=710)
selector: estimated_workspace(fused_paged_flash)=3.8GB > per-process limit 3.5GB -> choose flash_unfused
runtime: allocated fallback kernel; execution latency increased by 3.5x
```
jacob: Estimated workspace jumped on SM90 only? Did you repro on SM80?
maria: On SM80 with CUDA 12.2 the fused kernel stays selected and throughput is stable (~2k rps). So it's cross-arch + cuda combo.
ankit: CUDA 13 changed cuMemPool/alignment behaviour; could inflate "estimated scratch" because of pool rounding or new allocator alignment.
perf-bot: alert: perf-regression detected 2442108972 - sm90-paged-attn-qps-drop - 40% regression @p90
sasha: If estimator is conservative and forces fallback, we lose the runtime benefits of fused kernels despite higher workspace. Maybe the estimator model got tuned for sm80/12.x and isn't valid for sm90/13.x.
maria: Quick test: forced fused via REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=fused_paged_flash on canary SM90 -> throughput restored to ~2k rps, 95th latency back to baseline. So fused actually runs fine despite estimator warning.
jacob: Interesting — fused needs more workspace but runtime memory usage with KV streaming is lower due to reduced reads. Estimator may double-count worst-case scratch across buffers.
ankit: Can you paste calc outputs?
maria: 
```
calc_workspace(kernel=fused_paged_flash, seq=14000, bsz=8, sm=90) -> 3.8GB
calc_workspace(kernel=flash_unfused, seq=14000, bsz=8, sm=90) -> 1.1GB
measured_runtime_peak_mem(fused_paged_flash) -> 3.2GB
measured_runtime_peak_mem(flash_unfused) -> 3.9GB
```
sasha: So estimator overestimates fused but underestimates unfused when accounting for temporary buffers and KV caching interactions. Selector heuristic is using estimator-only and that's the problem.
ankit: Short-term mitigation: relax the workspace limit by x% for sm90+cuda13 combos and prefer empirically better kernels if we have probe data. Long-term: selector should calibrate per-arch+cuda with microbenchmarks.
maria: Proposal added in RW-3092: "selector: calibrate workspace vs measured peak at startup + maintain per-arch kernel perf table". Also add KV-aware warmup so selector doesn't flip during sustained warm KV use.
jacob: Also open ticket to triage cuMemPool behavior changes in CUDA13 (alignment/pool rounding). Might be why estimator math changed.
ankit: I'll draft a PR to add a small calibration task that runs once per machine type (takes ~30s) and writes calibration file to /var/lib/redwood/kernel_calib.json. Selector will consult it.
sasha: Also add a canary flag to force-fuse where safe. Then run dedicated canary fleet for sm90+13 with synthetic longctx to validate.
maria: RW-3092 has logs + perf graphs. I pinned the forced-fused canary to a small customer subset. Early results look promising.
ankit: Assigning follow-ups: RW-3093 (calibration PR) -> ankit, RW-3094 (cuda13 allocator triage) -> jacob, RW-3092 (investigation + canary) -> maria.
maria: Can we sync tomorrow 10am PT to roll the calibration to staging? :calendar: 
all: +1
